text:
Maya: Thanks everyone for the runtime section at today's all-hands. Quick follow-ups:

- KV cache eviction: do we use TTL or LRU for short-lived sessions? Impact on chat session freshness and cost?
- Can we get P50/P95/P99 numbers for microbatching latency (batch=8 vs 32) so product can reason about SLOs?
- Kernel rollout: what's the plan for model-variant fallbacks during canary and who owns rollbacks?

Anyone from leads/ops able to drop short answers here?

Devon: I'll take cache + latency numbers for now. Short answers until I paste slides:
Cache: TTL (default 30m) + size-based LRU eviction. For short-lived chat sessions we pin per-session prefixes for 2-5 minutes (configurable). That avoids noisy early-evictions for conversational state. We do NOT do global synchronous flushes except during major migrations.

Numbers (quick, infra median across gpu-pool-alpha):
- batch=8 -> p50 12ms, p95 38ms, p99 120ms
- batch=32 -> p50 18ms, p95 65ms, p99 240ms
These are for single-request single-token continuation; multi-token throughput behaves differently. I'll upload the slide with distributions. :thumbsup:

Sanjay: Rollout plan (ops summary): canary in us-west-2 at 5% traffic for 30m with detailed traces -> if stable, increase to eu-central 10% -> then global ramp. Fallback policy: runtime will auto-route to quantized-compatible model variant if latency exceeds target for 30s; automated rollback of control plane only triggers if error rate >1% or request failures hit threshold. We'll keep human-in-loop for irreversible DB migrations.

Olivia: Prewarm note — for workflows with long contexts we do a cheap KV prewarm on canary hosts using recent prompt-sets; that reduces p99 by ~25-35% in our tests. Prewarm is opt-in per route to avoid cold-start cost for low-traffic routes.

Priya: Ops checklist items to flag: set circuit-breaker thresholds (p99 latency 500ms or error rate 0.5%) to trigger partial traffic drain; ensure canary has dedicated logging retention and trace sampling at 100% for 30m. I'll create a ticket for the runbook and tabletop.

OpsBot: Canary created: canary/2198765432 scheduled 2026-04-02T15:00:00Z. Monitoring alert stream: runtime-canary-latency and runtime-canary-error.

Maya: thanks. Devon — can you paste the slide link and a config snippet? Sanjay — please add the rollback playbook link. Priya — assign the ticket to me so I can prep the leadership checklist.

Devon: Slide deck: https://docs.redwood.ai/slides/runtime-canary-q1 (will attach)
Quick config example for the cache + batching defaults:
```
cache:
  mode: ttl_lru
  ttl_seconds: 1800
  per_session_pin_seconds: 300
batching:
  default_max_batch: 32
  microbatch_targets: [8, 32]
  latency_goals_ms:
    p50: 20
    p95: 80
    p99: 250
```
(These are the current defaults; we iterate per workload.)

Sanjay: Rollback playbook (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/playbooks/runtime-rollback — contains steps for immediate rollback, partial drain, and postmortem timeline. Will add a blameless checklist and contact list.

Priya: Ticket created: R-9876 assigned to Maya. Tabletop exercise scheduled 2026-03-31 17:00 PT. Ops will run simulations of the fallback and eviction scenarios.

Maya: @everyone thanks — I'll follow up with a short doc summarizing this thread and link into the all-hands notes. If anyone wants to add short test prompts we should use for canary prewarm, drop them here and I'll collate.

Devon: dropping two quick test prompts — one short convo, one long context: "You are an assistant." and a 2048-token context with repeated persona lines.

Olivia: will add a small script to the canary repo to exercise prewarm flows.

Priya: adding ops-run checklist to the ticket now.

Maya: closing for now, will tag folks when docs are up. :sparkles:
